claims.statement: C2C-087 blocked on the pace-model re-fit for want of post-fix sessions. They arrived, and the answer is still 'cannot re-fit' -- but now for a measured reason. An OLS re-fit over 733 sessions gave 91.0 + 0.780/MB, a slope twice the shipped 0.376, suggesting systematic under-prediction. The binned residuals refute it directly: at that slope the 100-135 MB bucket should sit +46s against the shipped model and it measures +5.7s (n=141), so the 0.780 is pulled by a handful of high-leverage heavy captures. Three further findings came out of the same round: the pre-09-26 residuals are non-monotonic in capture size, and systematic model bias must be monotonic, so those residuals were real time-correlated degradation rather than bias -- which vindicates C2C-073's residual method; C2C-073's own +116.8s degradation is substantially the 300-second extraction timeout hitting large captures (+121.4s on the four cut-off sessions at 585 MB median, versus +0.1s on the 114 that completed); and my own alternative specification (overhead = inside minus planned span) measured worse, not better, because longer sessions capture more packets so the planned span correlates with MB. Disposition: none of VOLUME_FIXED_SEC, VOLUME_SLOPE_SEC_PER_MB, MODEL_INVALID_ABOVE_MB or SLOW_SESSION_SEC changed.

claims.statement: Relaxing a pass criterion is the operator's decision, so this one was measured, written up, and left alone until authorized. Basis: on a segment certified healthy by three non-temporal criteria (rc=0 44/44, 98.1 percent eligible, batches 40/40), the misfire rate falls from 1/80 to 0/80, and 90 is not arbitrary -- that segment's worst window sits at +69.1s, so any threshold between 60 and 69.1 cannot fix the one misfire. Cost: 87 windows fall in (60, 90] in a population whose health is not certified, so they cannot be classified as misfires or real degradation. Safety rests on the margin to real degradation: the degradation C2C-073 identified is +116.8s, and its physical substance -- the 178 sessions whose extraction was cut off -- sits at +256.0s median with 177 of 178 over the threshold. The round also nearly produced a silent failure: one constant served both the alarm threshold and the bound on model bias, and the rejected OLS re-fit is off by -68.9s at 200 MB, which is outside 60 but inside 90 -- so raising the single constant would have stopped a mutation test biting while all tests stayed green. The two concepts are now separate, pinned by a test that they must not be equal.

claims.statement: The supervisor logged 'enforce stack will not come up', and that sentence was wrong twice: the stack did come up -- seven nodes healthy, HMAC fingerprints matching -- and it was deliberately stopped. The chain: Gazebo's launch produced no process-started line within 118 seconds, the readiness probe gave up at its 120-second ceiling, the stack failed closed and stopped the group, and six processes each shut down twice. The supervisor's own poll window was 200 seconds, so it never got the chance to wait. Seen per round the failure is progressive -- rounds 1 to 3 fine in both modes, Enforce gone from round 4, Permissive also gone by rounds 7 and 9 -- and Enforce runs second, so it was eaten first. The three layers are now probe 240, wrapper 250, supervisor 300, pinned by tests that fix the ordering rather than the seconds, because changing one number alone is exactly how the inversion arose.
claims.title: The Enforce data gap was a three-layer readiness window inverted, and it was not Enforce-specific

claims.statement: Segmenting by fix date rather than evenly: the fork-teardown fix helped Permissive (13.2 to 7.0 percent) and did nothing for Enforce (34.0 to 34.7 percent), which agrees with C2C-089 -- the failure it fixed is now 2 of 599, and Enforce fails at startup. It is not evidence of zero: the next 80 sessions measured 5.0 percent, above the 3.7 percent rule-of-three bound I had published, and the combined figure is 4 of 160 or 2.5 percent, which the campaign has since reproduced at 12 of 473. Per-step timings place the residual stalls inside Node() and create_subscription with normal import times, which rules out the six parameter services, since those switches are in the code. claims.statement: N37 recorded its own blindness three times over -- a recon-line marker, a blind key on every decision-trace step, and a warning carrying the underlying RCLError -- and nothing downstream read any of them. Across the whole of dataset_mega, insider_parameter_write is blind 22 of 22 and insider_hmac_forgery 17 of 17, while every other scenario is 0 of 790, and a read-only audit over 2,053 complete sessions puts it at 113 blind of 1,524 determinable, all of them insider. The mechanism is the opposite of intuition: an uncredentialed outsider has no keystore, so security never engages and Node() succeeds, whereas a credentialed insider has a keystore and so, under Enforce, Node('n37_probe') needs an enclave that the fourteen do not include and fails closed. Partial credentials are stricter than none. That is the threat model working -- a thief of node X's credentials cannot also be n37_probe -- so the fix is recording, not granting the attacker an enclave it should not have.
claims.title: The adaptive attacker has never adapted in any credentialed-insider session, and the threat model is why

evidence.description: The refuted strong form, the confirmed weak form, the corrected pooling, and why the confound is structural rather than a defect

limitations: The volume figures are pcap bytes and packet counts, which are the source of the network features but not the feature values themselves.
The intensity figures come from the attacker's own decision trace, not an independent traffic measurement.

Both directions of the consequence -- that insider difficulty may be overstated, or that a model could learn low intensity implies insider -- are unproven, and deciding between them needs a sighted-insider session that the threat model does not permit.
claims.statement: The strong form is refuted: all 117 blind sessions have distinct first-three-step intensity sequences, as do 1,159 of 1,432 sighted ones, so the fixed cadence is jittered and leaves no memorizable fingerprint. The weak form holds with a clear direction: within-session intensity standard deviation is 0.0454 against 0.3351, a factor of 7.4, and step-six median intensity is 0.414 against 1.280 against a ceiling of 1.600 -- blind sessions never escalate, because escalation is conditioned on not having been noticed and an attacker that cannot see alerts can never confirm that. At the data level it weakens: pcap bytes come to 0.905 times and packets to 0.655 times, and insider_parameter_write at 129.4 MB sits mid-table among twenty scenarios. Mechanism-matched pairs are ambiguous, and my first pooling was wrong -- I put a flood scenario in the control for a parameter-write attack -- so the per-pair figures are 0.866 for parameter write and 0.572 to 0.752 for HMAC forgery. Attribution is structurally inseparable: blindness and insider status are perfectly collinear, and separating them would require granting the attacker the enclave that the previous claim says it must not have.
claims.title: The blindness confound is real at the attacker level, modest in the data, and not separable

claims.statement: Until now the identification half had an indivisible path and the open-set half had only refuse-to-overwrite, which a different output path walks past -- and the backlog records the previous holdout as spent three times. Two sub-judgements I offered were both wrong and were corrected by measurement: splitting the holdout in half is unnecessary because split and novelty_role are orthogonal (45 test sessions against 40 novelty with 6 overlapping), so one seal per scope coexist without blocking each other and open-once never needs loosening; and the two halves using different formulations is by design, because max_softmax and k-of-n were measured on the parallel-gate line, so the gap was only the seal. Rehearsing on the already-spent 2026-09-03 holdout caught three real defects: an uninformative refusal on the wrong metrics file, the seal's scope name compared against the feature column's value, and -- the consequential one -- a recall denominator that included the holdout sessions' normal rows, 161 of 537, because novelty_role marks whole sessions. Exclusion from fitting is session-level; evaluation is label-level.
claims.title: The open-set half goes through the seal, and rehearsing it caught a defect that would have spent the holdout on a wrong denominator
